clue.text: Massage for Asian holidaying in Africa?

indicators.note: to massage figures is to manipulate them, so the next words are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spa treatment offered for an Asian visitor, perhaps at a resort while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Massage' reads as a noun for the spa, but it is the signal to rearrange FOR ASIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a wildlife-viewing trip is the classic way to holiday in Africa, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: East European city where two vessels turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a wok is a cooking vessel
Noah's ark is a vessel, a boat

explanation.surface: A Polish city where a couple of boats appeared one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses WOKARK, read bottom to top in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish city, an old royal capital, is in central Europe's east, so a geographic description.

clue.text: University using leverage for the revolution

parts.note: prising a lid open is using leverage on it

explanation.surface: A university is putting pressure on, levering for change to bring about the revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular revolt against rulers is a revolution, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Wintry weather damaging ego, if cold

indicators.note: damaging the following letters breaks them and leaves them in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Freezing weather is hard on one's self-esteem when it's cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A freezing mist of ice crystals is a kind of winter weather in very cold places.

clue.text: Player in order, not entirely out of order

indicators.note: out of order means jumbled, so the remaining letters are shuffled
not all of the phrase in order is used: its final letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports player first in order, then not quite out of order, a referee's muddled ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts the last R of IN ORDER to give INORDE, which 'out of order' shuffles. Robert is the actor; 'Player' is used throughout this puzzle for film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a player, and Robert De Niro is a famous film actor.

clue.text: Player with a dozen legs, nineteen extremely ridiculous!

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters before it are made into a crazy new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of the word nineteen are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An actor playing a creature with twelve legs at nineteen: utterly absurd!
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes NN from nineteen; those join WITHADOZENLEGS and 'ridiculous' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a Hollywood actor, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Player — Yorkshire opener

parts.note: the dash stands for the gap that separates the word before it from the word after it

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket player described: he is the Yorkshire opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheeky: the dash is literally the gap between 'Player' and 'Yorkshire'. A cricket opener is a batsman who goes in first, which disguises 'opener' as the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin Spacey is a film actor, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Express suffering a shade

parts.note: to yell is to express loudly, cry out
ow is a cry that expresses pain or suffering

explanation.surface: Showing one's pain in some colour, or an express train suffering in shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Express suffering' is a shout of OW, a yelled cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a colour, and one hue or tint of colour is called a shade.

clue.text: Garbo? Somewhere in the theatre

parts.note: the actress's name splits as GARB (clothing) plus O (a ring shape); the answer's two words, read as clues, give those pieces

explanation.surface: Greta Garbo, the film star, might be found somewhere in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer's two words give GARB then O, which spell the actress's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first balcony tier of seats above the stalls in a theatre.

clue.text: Reveal odd characters in name while in Britain

indicators.note: being in Britain means sitting inside the letters for Britain

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain

indicators.note: the odd characters are the first and third letters of the word name

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as we spoke'

explanation.surface: Expose the strange people in a name while they are in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters in' picks letters 1 and 3; 'in' (the second one) is the container signal. 'while' as AS is a common crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask someone is to expose or reveal who they really are.

clue.text: Accumulation of water, a final burst splitting both ways

indicators.note: the anagram goes between R and L, splitting them apart

parts.note: both ways means right and left, R and L

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dam's water piling up until a last eruption splits it in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges A FINAL into AINFAL, and that splits R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain collected over a period is measured as the total amount of water that has come down.

clue.text: Margaret playing Jack, great player

parts.note: Meg is a short form of the name Margaret
an actor playing Hamlet is cast as Hamlet, so playing gives as
a jack tar, or simply jack, is a sailor, and so is a tar

explanation.surface: Margaret, cast as Jack in a play, gives a great performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge celebrity in film or music is a supreme star, a great player in the acting sense.

clue.text: See 5 down
Player casually getting agency bewildered by riddle

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Jimmy Riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, so riddle and jimmy both stand for a pee

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so the letters of agency are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor offhandedly getting his agent confused by a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' belongs with Player: the familiar form of the actor James Cagney's first name. Rhyming slang is Cockney: a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cagney was a Hollywood film actor, and the casual form of his first name gives this version.

clue.text: Mate, Brando?

parts.note: the actor's name splits as BRAND (a make of product) plus O (zero, a nil score in tennis); the answer's two words give those pieces

explanation.surface: Pal, Marlon Brando? A friendly hail to the famous actor.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the first word is a synonym of brand and the second the tennis zero, O, together spelling the actor's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to couple sexually, which is to have intercourse.

clue.text: Player bearing ash, perhaps?

parts.note: east is a compass bearing
ash is one example of a timber, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: An actor carrying ashes, perhaps after a cremation.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint Eastwood is a film actor, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Player with paintings of the ladies, possibly?

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, and bog is British slang for a toilet
paintings are art

explanation.surface: An actor holding paintings of women, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog art' would be paintings of (in) the ladies' toilet; BOG is British slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a film actor, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Player walkin' round

parts.note: pacing is walking, and the apostrophe drops the final G here too
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An actor strolling around in casual speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Pacino is a film actor, and an actor is a player.

clue.text: Other ranks following leadership of Kim in another bonkers nation

indicators.note: the K and OR go inside the scrambled letters
bonkers means mad, so the letters of another are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the other ranks come after the leading letter of Kim
the leadership of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops follow Kim's lead in yet another crazy state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonkers' turns ANOTHER into NORTHEA, and KOR goes inside it. Kim Jong-un is the country's leader, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sovereign state in East Asia, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Go first in test before scorer

indicators.note: the letter comes before the composer in the answer
the first letter in the word test is taken

parts.note: Ravel the composer wrote musical scores, so is a scorer

explanation.surface: Bat first in a Test match ahead of the run-scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a Test is an international match and a scorer records runs; 'scorer' is really a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go somewhere is to journey there, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A hero netting billions for England

indicators.note: the lion nets, or catches, the letter inside itself

parts.note: a brave hero is called a lion
B is a common abbreviation for billion(s)

explanation.surface: A heroic figure catching billions on England's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old poetic name for Britain or England, used in crosswords and verse.

clue.text: See 11
Similar slowing in spring, reversed

indicators.note: the musical slowing goes inside the turned spring
reversed means the word for spring is read backwards

parts.note: to spring is to leap
rall. is a musical direction, short for rallentando, meaning slowing down

explanation.surface: Much the same as getting slower in springtime, but backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns the synonym for spring backwards before the musical term goes 'in'. 'Spring' looks like the season but is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or events that run alongside and match are alike, so this means similar or corresponding.

clue.text: Cockney Asian's sound formal wear?

parts.note: a true Cockney is born within earshot of the bells of St Mary-le-Bow, in Bow in London

indicators.note: sound signals a word said aloud that is spelt differently

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian person from Thailand

explanation.surface: A Londoner's Asian friend's accent, when dressed up for a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are traditional working-class East Londoners, and Bow is the area tied to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow-shaped tie goes with a dinner jacket, an example of formal clothing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Figure in our hearts losing nothing after time

indicators.note: the phrase comes after the time letter

parts.note: we is the subject form of our, the people speaking

indicators.note: the word for nothing is lost from the phrase

parts.note: a heart symbol stands for love, as in I heart NY
O, zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A person who stays in our hearts though they lose nothing over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in our hearts' reads as 'we love'; 'losing nothing' drops O from the second word, and 'after time' puts it all behind T.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a figure, and this one is the number after eleven.

clue.text: Male briefly wearing jumper, elaborate in style

indicators.note: the jumper wears the male bird, holding it inside

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A man, briefly, in a sweater that is ornate in design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater (British for a knitted pullover) but is a kangaroo. 'briefly' drops a final letter; 'wearing' puts the male bird inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century ornate style of decoration with scrolls and shells is a byword for elaborate design.
